text:
alex: Hey all — first week here! Quick Q about Developer API keys / sandbox: how do I get a sandbox key, are there default quotas/rate limits, and what’s the recommended way to use keys in my local dev + CI?
maria: welcome alex :tada: — short answer: use the Console to create a dev (sandbox) key, it’s separate from prod keys and comes with free credits. Doc: https://console.redwood.ai/api-keys (Console -> API keys).
alex: awesome — is the sandbox key limited in lifetime? and are quotas very low by default?
maria: sandbox keys auto-expire after 90 days if unused (rotates to reduce leak risk). Default project quota for sandbox: 60 requests/min and 200k tokens/min aggregate (these are soft limits). Production keys have higher defaults based on plan. If you need more for load testing file a support request or ping @kevin.
kevin: yup — for larger quota or dedicated capacity we route through Sales/Infra. For quick increases (non-prod) we can bump sandbox quotas by request; prod increases require billing/commit. Also don’t use prod keys in CI or public repos.
sam: a few practical tips: 1) make a project in Console named like "team-<your-name>-dev" and generate a key labeled "local-dev". 2) store it in your OS keychain or .env (local only). 3) CI: add it as a secret in the repo (GH Actions: REDWOOD_API_KEY).
jordan: example of running a simple curl locally:```bash
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-sandbox-xxxx"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"rw-chat-sandbox","input":"hi"}'
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
alex: good call — any rate-limit headers to watch for so I can handle retries gracefully?
maria: yes we return standard `Retry-After` on 429s and headers like `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. If you see 429 in dev, reduce concurrency or batch inputs. For token-heavy workloads prefer smaller chunk sizes and streaming to stay under per-second throughput.
alex: who should I contact if my sandbox key gets leaked or I suspect misuse?
kevin: ping @security and rotate the key immediately (Console -> revoke). We can also revoke all keys on a project if needed. We recommend enabling audit logs on your dev project — that’s under Console -> Settings -> Audit.
sam: also pro tip: create a short-lived key for experiments and put it in `~/.config/redwood/credentials` in case you accidentally push env files — easier to rotate.
maria: if you want I can create a starter project for you with a sandbox key and sample GH Actions secret — alex, want me to do that?
alex: yes please that would be super helpful.
onboarding-bot: Welcome message sent to alex. Onboarding checklist updated: created ticket #ONB-183 for dev sandbox provisioning.
maria: done — I created project "alex-dev-sandbox" and added a key named "alex-local". I also dropped a short README in the project with the curl example and CI snippet. You should have an invite to the project in the Console.
alex: got it, I see the invite and key. thanks y’all! :heart:
jordan: and if you plan to run load tests, loop in infra/eng-sre first — they’ll advise on using Dedicated or simulated traffic so it doesn’t affect shared pool.
alex: noted. I'll start with small tests and escalate if needed. Thanks everyone!
